items.title: An extended certificate of small size is decided by the matchings it forces
items.author: Gilad Chase; Neta Dafni; Yuval Filmus; Nathan Lindzey
items.work: Uniqueness for 2-Intersecting Families of Permutations and Perfect Matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 694-696: for an extended certificate of size at most n minus two and a second certificate of the same size, if two matchings are related in the prescribed way and one of them fails the triple of the extended certificate while satisfying its pairs, then the other fails a specific pair of the second certificate. The proof (source lines 697-706) is a flip argument: the failing matching is normalised so that the offending pair joins the first two indices of the triple, the size bound guarantees at least three further pairs so that two alternative matchings can be built by crossing two pairs at a time, both alternatives avoid the three pairs of the triple, and the exclusion of the remaining possibilities forces the prescribed triple. The statement records the implication and none of the flipping.

proof_spans.label: the complete author proof of the labelled lemma, retained line for line
